title: Slow down near wet or shaded potholes
body: Standing water and tree shadows can hide deep road craters. Reduce speed to protect your tires, suspension, and nearby pedestrians from splashes.

title: Never drive through flooded drainage inlets
body: Moving floodwater over clogged drains can conceal open manholes or washed-out pavement. Reroute when water depth reaches curb height.

title: Stay alert on unlit barangay streets
body: Use low beams when approaching oncoming traffic and watch closely for pedestrians and cyclists along stretches with busted streetlights.

title: Run front and rear lights after dusk
body: Equip your bike with a steady white front light and a blinking red taillight so motorists can spot you early in poorly lit areas.

title: Check blind spots before swerving around hazards
body: Signal early and shoulder-check before steering wide around potholes, uneven concrete slabs, or clogged roadside grates.

title: Cross metal drain grates straight on
body: Wet steel grates become slick and narrow slots can catch thin tires. Approach squarely at a controlled speed.

title: Walk facing oncoming traffic on obstructed roads
body: When broken sidewalks or ongoing LGU repairs force you onto the road shoulder, walk facing traffic so you can see approaching vehicles.

title: Wear bright or reflective gear at night
body: Light-colored clothing or reflective strips make you visible from a safe braking distance along streets with dead streetlights.

title: Snap hazard photos from a safe distance
body: Step onto a safe sidewalk or curb before taking photos for AYOS—never stand in active traffic lanes to document road damage.
